National Weather Service Burlington VT
731 AM EDT Wed Oct 7 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
As of 229 PM EDT Tuesday...

Frost Advisory will end this morning for the Champlain Valley.
Timing for rain showers next week has been moved up earlier to 
Sunday evening.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
As of 227 AM EDT Wednesday...

1. Showery conditions developing for the rest of the week.

2. Dry and seasonable weekend before showers return for the 
beginning of next week.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
As of 227 AM EDT Wednesday...

KEY MESSAGE 1: A warm front will push east across the area with 
relatively little fanfare. Mid-level dry air is expected to limit 
shower activity as it lifts northeast this morning. Moderation 
behind the front will push temperatures into the 60s for most today, 
but with a few spot 50s still in the Northeast Kingdom. Today's main 
story will be the strong south to southwesterly winds that develop. 
Modest mixing behind the warm front will bring 20-30 mph wind gusts, 
locally to 35 mph on the northern slopes of the Dacks near Malone, 
NY and then near the shores of Lake Champlain. A prefrontal trough 
will begin to track east towards the St. Lawrence Valley later this 
evening. Then, it'll translate to Vermont overnight. Showers will 
track east along the feature, with a greater concentration over 
northern New York where better dynamics and moisture lies that will 
degrade heading into Vermont. By Thursday morning, temperatures will 
begin to cool aloft as an upper low digs southeastwards. Surface 
pressures will lower as the upper vort swings in, and this could 
continue to generate showers across the area. This will set up 
Thursday afternoon to be convective. The combination of a 
strengthening cold front as a 1001-1002mb low tracks just north of 
Montreal, mid-level cooling, and surface temperatures in the 60s 
will allow for the dynamic system to take advantage of around 250-
500 J/kg of CAPE across the area. Like Monday, we may have some pea-
sized hail and isolated thunder on Thursday afternoon, with the 
greatest likelihood near the international border.

Temperatures will sink back near to below seasonal norms in the 50s 
to near 60 for Friday. The post-frontal air mass will still be 
beneath a broad upper low, and some spot showers remain possible 
Friday afternoon. The backside of the upper trough will start 
sliding east by Friday night. This will allow for one night of 
radiational cooling and frost potential again in the Champlain 
Valley. A few additional spot showers will be possible as warm 
advection begins to nose in heading into Saturday, but nothing 
significant is expected.

KEY MESSAGE 2: Surface high pressure builds in for the weekend, leading 
to a couple classic fall days. Highs will be in the 50s and 60s with 
mostly sunny skies. The remnants of what will likely become Isaias 
looks to move into the region to start next week. The center of the 
low should track well to the south, but periods of showers and 
potentially an area of stratiform rain are increasingly likely for 
Monday and Tuesday. By the time it reaches the region, it will have 
weakened significantly so any rainfall will remain beneficial 
and there will be no wind threat. The next cold front passes 
through mid- week, bringing more potential showers. Overall, 
temperatures will be relatively seasonable, with slightly above 
average temperatures to start the week and slightly below 
average temperatures to end the week.

&&

.AVIATION /12Z WEDNESDAY THROUGH SUNDAY/...
Through 12Z Thursday...VFR conditions are expected to mostly persist
for the next 24 hours. The only exceptions could be late this
afternoon and late tonight when a few showers move through. While
most of them will be too light to cause significant visibility
reductions, a brief drop to MVFR visibility is possible. This
afternoon, that would likely only occur over northern New York 
but late tonight, that could occur at any terminal. Winds will 
become southerly to southwesterly and increase quickly this 
morning. Gusts in the 15-30 KT range are expected during the 
day, with the strongest gusts at BTV, PBG and MSS. Winds will 
decrease a bit this evening and by 06Z, the gusts should mostly 
be below 20 KT. LLWS is expected to develop in places this 
evening, especially in Vermont outside the Champlain Valley.

Outlook...

Thursday: VFR. Chance SHRA, Slight chance TSRA.
Thursday Night: VFR. Chance SHRA.
Friday: VFR. Slight chance SHRA.
Friday Night: VFR. NO SIG WX.
Saturday: VFR. NO SIG WX.
Saturday Night: VFR. NO SIG WX.
Sunday: VFR. NO SIG WX.

&&

.MARINE...
A Lake Wind Advisory will be in effect over Lake Champlain
beginning later this morning. Winds are expected to increase 
behind a warm front that will pass through without much
precipitation. South winds of 15 to 25 knots will arrive around
10 AM and peak just under 30 knots over the broad waters by mid
afternoon before decreasing very slowly. Waves are expected to 
build up to 2 to 4 feet, with values closer to 3 to 5 feet over 
the broad waters. Lingering 2 to 4 foot waves are likely during 
the evening.

&&

.BTV WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
VT...None.
NY...None.

&&

$$
